title: The Case of the Wandering Key
story: Otis keeps the spare lighthouse key on a hook in the harbor office. One November Thursday the hook sat empty, and by Friday morning the key was quietly back, as if it had never left. Five people visited the office that Thursday, each at a different hour, on a different errand, standing in a different spot. The hook is on the key wall, and only someone at that wall could have lifted the key unseen. Who borrowed the spare key?

texts: The visitor by the window is neither Nadia nor Sam.
Teddy asked about either the tide chart or the radio.
Sam stood by either the window or the map table.
The visitor who asked about the permit came in at either noon or 1:00 p.m.
Of the visitor who asked about the lost cap and the visitor by the desk, one came in at 9:00 a.m. and the other came in at 10:00 a.m.
Of the visitor by the window and the visitor who came in at 10:00 a.m., one asked about the lost cap and the other asked about the permit.
The visitor who came in at noon asked about neither the radio nor the permit.
The visitor who asked about the radio came in later than the visitor by the stove.
Sam came in earlier than Teddy.
Of Lena and the visitor who asked about the mooring fee, one came in at 10:00 a.m. and the other came in at 9:00 a.m.
